p0.original: Introduction to Poverty and Economic Inequality
p0.zh: 贫穷和经济不平等简介

p3.original: In September 2011, a group of protesters gathered in Zuccotti Park in New York City to decry what they perceived as increasing social and economic inequality in the United States. Calling their protest “Occupy Wall Street,” they argued that the concentration of wealth among the richest 1% in the United States was both economically unsustainable and inequitable, and needed to be changed. The protest then spread to other major cities, and the Occupy movement was born.
p3.zh: 2011年9月,一群抗议者聚集在纽约市的祖科蒂公园,谴责他们认为美国日益加剧的社会和经济不平等. 他们称他们的抗议为“占领华尔街 ” , 认为财富集中在美国最富有的1%的财富中既经济上不可持续,又不公平,需要改变。抗议随后蔓延到其他主要城市,占领运动诞生.

p4.original: Why were people so upset? How much wealth is concentrated among the top 1% in our society? How did they acquire so much wealth? These are very real, very important questions in the United States now, and this chapter on poverty and economic inequality will help us address the causes behind this sentiment.
p4.zh: 为什么人们会这么不高兴?多少财富集中在我们社会中的1%前列? 他们怎么得到这么多的财富? 这些是美国现在非常真实,非常重要的问题,关于贫穷和经济不平等的这一章将有助于我们解决这种情绪背后的根源。

p12.original: The labor markets that determine the pay that workers receive do not take into account how much income a family needs for food, shelter, clothing, and health care. Market forces do not worry about what happens to families when a major local employer goes out of business. Market forces do not take time to contemplate whether those who are earning higher incomes should pay an even higher share of taxes.
p12.zh: 决定工人工资的劳动力市场没有考虑到家庭对食物、住所、衣物和保健需要多少收入。市场力量并不担心当当地主要雇主停业时,家庭会怎样。市场力量不花时间来考虑那些收入较高的人是否应该缴纳更高份额的税。

p13.original: However, labor markets do create considerable income inequalities. In 2020, the median American household income was $67,521 (the median is the level where half of all families had more than that level and half had less). For family households, the median was $86,372; for non-family households, it was $40,464. The Census Bureau also reported that in 2020, there were 37.2 million people living in poverty, representing 11.4% of the population. Think about a family of three—perhaps a single mother with two children—attempting to pay for the basics of life on perhaps $17,916 per year. After paying for rent, healthcare, clothing, and transportation, such a family might have $6,000 to spend on food. Spread over 365 days, the food budget for the entire family would be about $17 per day. To put this in perspective, most cities have restaurants where $17 will buy you an appetizer for one.
p13.zh: 然而,劳动力市场确实造成了相当大的收入不平等。2020年,美国家庭收入中位数为67,521美元(中位数是所有家庭中有一半家庭收入高于该水平,一半家庭收入低于该水平).家庭家庭的中位数为86 372美元;非家庭家庭的中位数为40 464美元。人口调查局还报告说,2020年,共有3,720万人生活贫困,占人口的11.4%。考虑一个由三个人组成的家庭——也许有一个有两个孩子的单身母亲——试图每年支付17 916美元的生活基本费用。 在支付房租、医疗、衣物和交通费之后,这样的家庭可能有6 000美元用于食品。 在365天的时间内,整个家庭的食品预算约为每天17美元。大部分城市都有餐厅 17美元会给你买开胃菜

p14.original: This chapter explores how the U.S. government defines poverty, the balance between assisting the poor without discouraging work, and how federal antipoverty programs work. It also discusses income inequality—how economists measure inequality, why inequality has changed in recent decades, the range of possible government policies to reduce inequality, and the danger of a tradeoff that too great a reduction in inequality may reduce incentives for producing output.
p14.zh: 本章探讨美国政府如何定义贫困,在援助穷人而不阻碍工作之间如何平衡,以及联邦除贫方案如何运作. 报告还讨论了收入不平等——经济学家如何衡量不平等,为何不平等在近几十年中发生了变化,政府减少不平等的可能政策的范围,以及权衡是否过度减少不平等可能减少生产产出的激励因素的危险。

p16.original: Comparisons of high and low incomes raise two different issues: economic inequality and poverty. Poverty is measured by the number of people who fall below a certain level of income—called the poverty line—that defines the income one needs for a basic standard of living. Measures of inequality compare the shares of a nation's income or wealth that comparable groups receive. A common inequality measure is Income inequality. One of numerous ways to look at income inequality is to compare the share of income that the top 10% receive to the share of income that the bottom 10% receive.
p16.zh: 高收入和低收入的比较提出了两个不同的问题:经济不平等和贫穷。贫穷的衡量标准是低于一定收入水平(即所谓的贫困线)的人数,而贫困线决定了人们的基本生活水准需要的收入。衡量不平等的措施比较了可比群体获得的国家收入或财富的份额。一种常见的不平等措施是收入不平等。审视收入不平等的多种途径之一是比较前10%的收入份额与后10%的收入份额。

p17.original: In the United States, the official definition of the poverty line traces back to a single person: Mollie Orshansky. In 1963, Orshansky, who was working for the Social Security Administration, published an article called “Children of the Poor” in a highly useful and dry-as-dust publication called the Social Security Bulletin. Orshansky’s idea was to define a poverty line based on the cost of a healthy diet.
p17.zh: 在美国,贫困线的官方定义追溯到一个人:莫利·奥尔尚斯基(Mollie Orshansky).1963年,为社会保障管理局工作的Orshansky在名为《社会保障公报》的非常有用和干燥的刊物上发表了一篇名为“穷人儿童”的文章。Orshansky的想法是,根据健康饮食的成本确定贫困线。

p18.original: Her previous job had been at the U.S. Department of Agriculture, where she had worked in an agency called the Bureau of Home Economics and Human Nutrition. One task of this bureau had been to calculate how much it would cost to feed a nutritionally adequate diet to a family. Orshansky found that the average family spent one-third of its income on food. She then proposed that the poverty line be the amount one requires to buy a nutritionally adequate diet, given the size of the family, multiplied by three.
p18.zh: 她以前的工作是在美国。农业部,她曾在一个名为家政和人类营养局的机构工作。该局的一项任务是计算向家庭提供营养充足的食物的费用。奥尔尚斯基发现,平均家庭将收入的三分之一花在了食物上. 她随后提议,鉴于家庭的规模,贫困线是购买营养充足的膳食所需的数额乘以3。

p19.original: The current U.S. poverty line is essentially the same as the Orshansky poverty line, although the government adjusts the dollar amounts to represent the same buying power over time. The U.S. poverty line in 2021 ranged from $12,880 for a single individual to $26,500 for a household of four people.
p19.zh: 目前的美国贫困线与奥尔尚斯基贫困线基本相同,不过政府调整美元金额,以表示随着时间的推移相同的购买力.2021年的美国贫困线从一个人12,880美元到4人家庭26,500美元不等.

p20.original: shows the U.S. poverty rate over time; that is, the percentage of the population below the poverty line in any given year. The poverty rate declined through the 1960s, rose in the early 1980s and early 1990s, but seems to have been slightly lower since the mid-1990s. However, in no year in the last six decades has the poverty rate been less than 10.5% of the U.S. population—that is, at best almost one American in nine is below the poverty line. In recent years, the poverty rate peaked at 15.1% in 2010, before dropping to 10.5% in 2019.  compares poverty rates for different groups in 2011. As you will see when we delve further into these numbers, poverty rates are relatively low for White people, for the elderly, for the well-educated, and for male-headed households. Poverty rates for females, Hispanic people, and African Americans are much higher than for White people. While Hispanic people and African Americans have a higher percentage of individuals living in poverty than others, most people in the United States living below the poverty line are White people.
p20.zh: 显示美国长期贫困率;即任何一年中贫困线以下人口的百分比。贫困率在1960年代一直下降,1980年代初和1990年代初有所上升,但自1990年代中期以来似乎略有下降。 然而,在过去60年中,没有一年的美国人口贫困率低于10.5%,也就是说,最多有九分之一的美国人生活在贫困线以下。 近年来,2010年的贫困率达到顶峰,达到15.1%,2019年降至10.5%. 相比2011年不同群体的贫困率. 当我们深入探讨这些数字时,你会看到,白人、老年人、受过良好教育的人和男性为户主的家庭的贫困率相对较低。女性、西班牙人和非裔美国人的贫困率远高于白人。 虽然西班牙裔人和非裔美国人生活在贫困中的人的比例高于其他人,但美国生活在贫困线以下的人大多是白人.

p44.original: The concept of a poverty line raises many tricky questions. In a vast country like the United States, should there be a national poverty line? After all, according to the Federal Register, the median household income for a family of four was $109,113 in New Jersey and $59,701 in Mississippi in 2017, and prices of some basic goods like housing are quite different between states. The poverty line is based on cash income, which means it does not account for government programs that provide non-cash assistance such as Medicaid (health care for low-income individuals and families) and food aid. Also, low-income families can qualify for federal housing assistance. (We will discuss these and other government aid programs in detail later in this chapter.)
p44.zh: 贫困线的概念提出了许多棘手的问题。在美国这样的广大国家里,是否应该有国家贫困线?毕竟,根据联邦注册局的数据,新泽西州4户家庭的平均家庭收入为109,113美元,密西西比州为59,701美元,州与州之间一些基本商品如住房的价格相差很大.贫困线以现金收入为基础,这意味着它不计入提供非现金援助的政府方案,如医疗补助(低收入个人和家庭的保健)和粮食援助。 此外,低收入家庭也有资格获得联邦住房援助。(我们将在本章后面详细讨论这些和其他政府援助方案。 )

p45.original: Should the government adjust the poverty line to account for the value of such programs? Many economists and policymakers wonder whether we should rethink the concept of what poverty means in the twenty-first century. The following Clear It Up feature explains the poverty lines set by the World Bank for low-income countries around the world.
p45.zh: 政府是否应该调整贫困线,以考虑这些方案的价值? 许多经济学家和决策者想知道,我们是否应该重新考虑贫穷在二十一世纪意味着什么的概念。 以下的Clear Up特征解释了世界银行为世界各地低收入国家设定的贫困线。

p47.original: The World Bank sets two poverty lines for low-income countries around the world. One poverty line is set at an income of $1.90/day per person. The other is at $3.20/day. By comparison, the U.S. 2015 poverty line of $20,090 annually for a family of three works out to $18.35 per person per day.
p47.zh: 世界银行为世界各地的低收入国家设定了两条贫困线。一条贫困线定为每人每天1.90美元。另一款为每日3.20美元。相较之下,美国.2015年3户家庭的贫困线为每年20,090元,每人每天18.35元.

p48.original: Clearly, many people around the world are far poorer than Americans, as  shows. China and India both have more than a billion people; Nigeria is the most populous country in Africa; and Egypt is the most populous country in the Middle East. In all four of those countries, in the mid-2000s, a substantial share of the population subsisted on less than $2/day. About half the world lives on less than $2.50 a day, and 80 percent of the world lives on less than $10 per day. (Of course, the cost of food, clothing, and shelter in those countries can be very different from those costs in the United States, so the $2 and $2.50 figures may mean greater purchasing power than they would in the United States.)
p48.zh: 显然,全世界许多人都比美国人穷得多,如前所述。 中国和印度的人口都超过10亿;尼日利亚是非洲人口最多的国家;埃及是中东人口最多的国家. 在其中所有四个国家,在2000年代中期,相当一部分人口每天生活费不到2美元。世界上约有一半人每天靠不到2.50美元生活,世界上80%的人每天靠不到10美元生活。(当然,这些国家的食品、衣物和住房费用可能与美国的费用有很大不同,因此,2美元和2.50美元的数字可能意味着比美国购买力更大。 )

p78.original: Any poverty line will be somewhat arbitrary, and it is useful to have a poverty line whose basic definition does not change much over time. If Congress voted every few years to redefine poverty, then it would be difficult to compare rates over time. After all, would a lower poverty rate change the definition, or is it the case that people were actually better off? Government statisticians at the U.S. Census Bureau have ongoing research programs to address questions like these.
p78.zh: 任何贫困线都有些武断,因此,制定一条贫困线是有用的,其基本定义不会随着时间推移而发生很大变化。 如果国会每几年投票一次,重新定义贫困,那么就很难在一段时间内比较贫困率.归根结底,降低贫困率是否会改变定义,还是人们实际上生活更好? 美国的政府统计学家.人口普查局有不断的研究方案来解决这类问题。

p80.original: Wages are influenced by Supply and demand in labor markets influence wages. This can lead to very low incomes for some people and very high incomes for others. Poverty and income inequality are not the same thing. Poverty applies to the condition of people who cannot afford the necessities of life. Income inequality refers to the disparity between those with higher and lower incomes. The poverty rate is what percentage of the population lives below the poverty line, which the amount of income that it takes to purchase the necessities of life determines. Choosing a poverty line will always be somewhat controversial.

p109.original: Can you give people too much help, or the wrong kind of help? When people are provided with food, shelter, healthcare, income, and other necessities, assistance may reduce their incentive to work, particularly if their work is likely to offer low wages and reduce government assistance. Consider a program to fight poverty that works in this reasonable-sounding manner: the government provides assistance to the those who need it, but as the recipients earn income to support themselves, the government reduces the level of assistance it provides. With such a program, every time a person earns $100, they lose $100 in government support. As a result, the person experiences no net gain for working. Economists call this problem the poverty trap.
p109.zh: 你能给别人太多的帮助, 还是错误的帮助? 如果向人们提供食物、住房、保健、收入和其他必需品,援助可能会减少他们的工作动力,特别是如果他们的工作有可能提供低工资和减少政府援助的话。考虑一个以这种合理方式开展工作的消除贫困方案:政府向需要援助的人提供援助,但随着受援者赚取收入以维持生计,政府减少了其提供的援助水平。有了这样的计划,每当一个人挣100美元,他们就会失去100美元的政府支持. 因此,此人的工作没有净收益。经济学家称这个问题为贫困陷阱.

p110.original: Consider the situation a single-parent family faces.  illustrates a single mother (earning $8 an hour) with two children. First, consider the labor-leisure budget constraint that this family faces in a situation without government assistance. On the horizontal axis is hours of leisure (or time spent with family responsibilities) increasing in quantity from left to right. Also on the horizontal axis is the number of hours at paid work, going from zero hours on the right to the maximum of 2,500 hours on the left. On the vertical axis is the amount of income per year rising from low to higher amounts of income. The budget constraint line shows that at zero hours of leisure and 2,500 hours of work, the maximum amount of income is $20,000 ($8 × 2,500 hours). At the other extreme of the budget constraint line, an individual would work zero hours, earn zero income, but enjoy 2,500 hours of leisure. At point A on the budget constraint line, by working 40 hours a week, 50 weeks a year, the utility-maximizing choice is to work a total of 2,000 hours per year and earn $16,000.
p110.zh: 考虑单亲家庭的处境,说明一个单身母亲(每小时挣8美元)有两个孩子。 首先,考虑这个家庭在没有政府援助的情况下所面临的劳动-劳动保障预算限制。横向轴线上是休闲时间(或承担家庭责任的时间)从左到右增加。横向轴线上还有有偿工作小时数,从右侧零小时到左侧最长2 500小时不等。 在纵向轴线上,是年收入从低到高的数额。预算限制线显示,在零小时闲暇和2 500小时工作时,收入最高额为20 000美元(8x2 500小时)。 在预算限制线的另一端,一个人将工作零小时,赚取零收入,但享受2 500小时的闲暇。 在预算限制线的A点,通过每周40小时、每年50周的工作,公用事业最大化的选择是每年总共工作2 000小时,赚取16 000美元。

p142.original: The new budget line, with the antipoverty program in place, is the horizontal and heavy line that is flat at $18,000. If the mother does not work at all, she receives $18,000, all from the government. If she works full time, giving up 40 hours per week with her children, she still ends up with $18,000 at the end of the year. Only if she works 2,300 hours in the year—which is an average of 44 hours per week for 50 weeks a year—does household income rise to $18,400. Even in this case, all of her year’s work means that household income rises by only $400 over the income she would receive if she did not work at all. She would need to work 50 hours a week to reach $20,800.
p142.zh: 新的预算项目,随着除贫方案的出台,是水平线和重线,平面为18 000美元。 如果母亲完全不工作,她就能得到18,000美元,全部来自政府. 如果她全天工作,放弃每周40小时与孩子一起工作,到年底她仍然以18000美元告终.只有当她一年工作2 300小时——平均每年工作50周,每周工作44小时——家庭收入才增加到18 400美元。 即使在这种情况下,她一年的全部工作都意味着如果她根本不工作,家庭收入只比她将获得的收入增加400美元。 她需要每周工作50小时,达到20 800美元。

p143.original: The poverty trap is even stronger than this simplified example shows, because a working mother will have extra expenses like clothing, transportation, and child care that a nonworking mother will not face, making the economic gains from working even smaller. Moreover, those who do not work fail to build up job experience and contacts, which makes working in the future even less likely.
p143.zh: 贫困陷阱比这个简化的例子更强大,因为工作母亲将获得额外开支,如衣物、交通和儿童保育,而非工作母亲不会面对这些开支,从而使从工作中获得的经济收益更小。 此外,那些不工作的人没有积累工作经验和建立联系,因此今后工作的可能性就更小。

p144.original: To reduce the poverty trap the government could design an antipoverty program so that, instead of reducing government payments by $1 for every $1 earned, the government would reduce payments by some smaller amount instead. Imposing requirements for work as a condition of receiving benefits and setting a time limit on benefits can also reduce the harshness of the poverty trap.
p144.zh: 为了减少贫困陷阱,政府可以设计一个消除贫困方案,这样,政府不会每挣1美元减少1美元,而会减少一些较小的金额。规定工作要求作为领取福利的条件,并对福利规定时限,也可以减轻贫困陷阱的严酷性。

p145.original: illustrates a government program that guarantees $18,000 in income, even for those who do not work at all, but then reduces this amount by 50 cents for each $1 earned. The new, higher budget line in  shows that, with this program, additional hours of work will bring some economic gain. Because of the reduction in government income when an individual works, an individual earning $8.00 will really net only $4.00 per hour. The vertical intercept of this higher budget constraint line is at $28,000 ($18,000 + 2,500 hours × $4.00 = $28,000). The horizontal intercept is at the point on the graph where $18,000 and 2500 hours of leisure is set.  shows the total income differences with various choices of labor and leisure.
p145.zh: 说明一项政府方案,该方案保证收入18 000美元,即使那些根本不工作的人也是如此,但随后每挣1美元减少50美分的收入。新的、更高的预算项目表明,通过这一方案,增加工作时间将带来一些经济收益。 由于个人工作时政府收入的减少,个人收入8美元实际上将只有每小时4.00美元的净值. 这一较高的预算限制线的垂直截击量为28 000美元(18 000美元+2 500小时x4.00美元=28 000美元)。横向截击就在图中设定了1.8万和2500小时的休闲时间,显示了收入总额与各种劳动和休闲选择的差别.

p146.original: However, this type of program raises other issues. First, even if it does not eliminate the incentive to work by reducing government payments by $1 for every $1 earned, enacting such a program may still reduce the incentive to work. At least some people who would be working 2,000 hours each year without this program might decide to work fewer hours but still end up with more income—that is, their choice on the new budget line would be like S, above and to the right of the original choice P. Of course, others may choose a point like R, which involves the same amount of work as P, or even a point to the left of R that involves more work.
p146.zh: 然而,这类方案也提出了其他问题。 首先,即使它通过将政府每1美元所得的付款减少1美元来消除工作的积极性,颁布这样一个方案仍然可能减少工作的积极性。 至少有些没有这个计划每年工作2 000小时的人可能决定减少工作时间,但最终还是有更多的收入,也就是说,他们在新预算项目上的选择与S,以上和原选择P的权利相同。 当然,其他人可能选择像R一样的点,它涉及与P相同的工作量,甚至R左侧的点,它涉及更多的工作.

p147.original: The second major issue is that when the government phases out its support payments more slowly, the antipoverty program costs more money. Still, it may be preferable in the long run to spend more money on a program that retains a greater incentive to work, rather than spending less money on a program that nearly eliminates any gains from working.
p147.zh: 第二个主要问题是,当政府更缓慢地逐步取消其支助付款时,除贫方案需要更多的资金。 然而,从长远来看,最好将更多的钱花在一个能保持更大工作动力的方案上,而不是把更少的钱花在一个几乎消除任何工作收益的方案上。

p178.original: The next module will consider a variety of government support programs focused specifically on people experiencing poverty, including welfare, SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program), Medicaid, and the earned income tax credit (EITC). p180.original: A poverty trap occurs when government-support payments decline as the recipients earn more income. As a result, the recipients do not end up with much more income when they work, because the loss of government support largely or completely offsets any income that one earns by working. Phasing out government benefits more slowly, as well as imposing requirements for work as a condition of receiving benefits and a time limit on benefits can reduce the harshness of the poverty trap.
p180.zh: 当受援者赚取更多收入时,政府支助付款减少,便会出现贫穷陷阱。 因此,领取者在工作时的收入不会多得多,因为政府支助的丧失在很大程度上或完全抵消了一个人通过工作赚取的任何收入。更缓慢地逐步取消政府福利,以及将工作要求作为领取福利的条件和对福利的时间限制,可以减轻贫困陷阱的严酷性。

p196.original: The U.S. government has implemented a number of programs to assist those below the poverty line and those who have incomes just above the poverty line. Such programs are called the safety net, to recognize that they offer some protection for those who find themselves without jobs or income.
p196.zh: 美国政府实施了若干方案,帮助那些生活在贫困线以下的人和那些收入刚刚高于贫困线的人。 这类方案被称为安全网,以承认它们为那些没有工作或收入的人提供了一些保护。

p198.original: From the Great Depression until 1996, the United States’ most visible antipoverty program was Aid to Families with Dependent Children (AFDC), which provided cash payments to mothers with children who were below the poverty line. Many just called this program “welfare.” In 1996, Congress passed and President Bill Clinton signed into law the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act, more commonly called the “welfare reform act.” The new law replaced AFDC with Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF).
p198.zh: 从大萧条到1996年,美国最引人注目的脱贫方案是援助有受抚养子女家庭(AFDC),向有子女但生活在贫困线以下的母亲提供现金支付.许多人刚刚称这个计划为“福利 ” 。 1996年,国会通过了《个人责任和工作机会和解法》,克林顿总统签署了该法案,成为法律。 该法案通常称为“福利改革法 ” 。 新法律用对贫困家庭的临时援助取代了AFDC。

p199.original: Visit this website to watch a video of President Bill Clinton’s Welfare Reform speech.
p199.zh: 访问该网站观看比尔·克林顿总统福利改革演讲的视频.

p200.original: TANF brought several dramatic changes in how welfare operated. Under the old AFDC program, states set the level of welfare benefits that they would pay to people experiencing poverty, and the federal government guaranteed it would chip in some of the money as well. The federal government’s welfare spending would rise or fall depending on the number of people in need, and on how each state set its own welfare contribution.
p200.zh: TANF在福利运作方式方面带来了一些巨大的变化。 根据旧的AFDC计划,各州设定了他们将向穷人支付的福利福利水平,联邦政府也保证将部分资金投入其中。联邦政府的福利开支会根据需要援助的人数以及各州如何确定自己的福利缴款情况而增加或减少。

p201.original: Under TANF, however, the federal government gives a fixed amount of money to each state. The state can then use the money for almost any program with an antipoverty component: for example, the state might use the money to give funds to families with low income, or to reduce teenage pregnancy, or even to raise the high school graduation rate. However, the federal government imposed two key requirements. First, if states are to keep receiving the TANF grants, they must impose work requirements so that most of those receiving TANF benefits are working (or attending school). Second, no one can receive TANF benefits with federal money for more than a total of five years over their lifetime. The old AFDC program had no such work requirements or time limits.
p201.zh: 然而,在TANF下,联邦政府给每个州固定数额的资金. 然后,国家可以把这笔钱用于几乎所有有消除贫困内容的方案:例如,国家可以把这笔钱用于向低收入家庭提供资金,或减少少女怀孕,甚至提高高中毕业率。 然而,联邦政府规定了两项关键要求。 首先,如果各州要继续领取过渡家庭补助,它们必须规定工作要求,以便大多数领取过渡家庭补助的人能够工作(或上学)。 第二,任何人都不能在一生中总共获得五年以上的联邦资金,领取TANF福利。旧的AFDC方案没有这种工作要求或时限。

p202.original: TANF attempts to avoid the poverty trap by requiring that welfare recipients work and by limiting the length of time they can receive benefits. In its first few years, the program was quite successful. The number of families receiving payments in 1995, the last year of AFDC, was 4.8 million. November 2020, according to the Congressional Research Service, the number of families receiving payments under TANF was 1.0 million—a decline of nearly 80%.
p202.zh: 过渡家庭基金会试图通过要求福利领取者工作并限制他们领取福利的时间来避免贫困陷阱。 在它的最初几年里,这个计划相当成功.1995年是非洲家庭发展基金的最后一年,领取津贴的家庭数量为480万。2020年11月,根据国会研究服务局的统计,根据TANF领取付款的家庭数量为100万个,下降了近80%.

p203.original: TANF benefits to poor families vary considerably across states. For example, again according to the Congressional Research Service, in July 2020 the highest monthly payment in New Hampshire to a single mother with one child was $862, while in Mississippi the highest monthly payment to that family was $146. In part, these payments reflect differences in states’ cost of living. As reported by the Department of Health and Human Services, in 1995 total spending on TANF was approximately $19 billion.  Spending increased yearly through 2001, then it was roughly flat at approximately $26 billion until 2005, then it increased again through 2010, where it peaked at nearly $35 billion. It then decreased again to around $30 billion in 2020. When you take into account the effects of inflation, the decline is even greater. Moreover, there seemed little evidence that families were suffering a reduced standard of living as a result of TANF—although, on the other side, there was not much evidence that families had greatly improved their total levels of income, either.
p203.zh: 各州对贫困家庭的过渡家庭补助差别很大。 例如,根据国会研究处的数据,2020年7月,新罕布什尔州向一个孩子的单身母亲支付的最高月薪为862美元,密西西比州对该家庭的月薪最高为146美元。 这些付款部分反映了各州生活费用的差异。卫生与公众服务部报告说,1995年,TANF的总开支约为190亿美元。整个2001年,开支每年增加,到2005年,大约为260亿美元,到2010年又增加,2010年达到顶峰,达到近350亿美元。之后又在2020年再次降至300亿美元左右.考虑通货膨胀的影响时,下降幅度更大. 此外,似乎没有多少证据表明家庭由于TANF而生活水平下降,虽然另一方面,也没有多少证据表明家庭也大大改善了总收入水平。

p205.original: The earned income tax credit (EITC), first passed in 1975, is a method of assisting the working poor through the tax system. The EITC is one of the largest assistance program for low-income groups, and as of December 2021, about 25 million eligible workers and families received about $60 billion in EITC. For the 2021 tax year, the earned income credit ranges from $1,502 to $6,728 depending on tax-filing status, income, and number of children. The average amount of EITC received nationwide was about $2,411. In 2021, for example, a single parent with two children would have received a tax credit of $5,980 up to a modest income level. The amount of the tax break increases with the amount of income earned, up to a point. The earned income tax credit has often been popular with both economists and the general public because of the way it effectively increases the payment received for work.
p205.zh: 1975年首次通过的所得所得税抵免是通过税收制度帮助有工作的穷人的一种方法。EITC是针对低收入群体的最大的援助方案之一,截至2021年12月,约2500万符合条件的工人和家庭在EITC中获得了约600亿美元.2021纳税年度,根据纳税申报状况,收入,子女数量等因素,所得收入抵免额从1,502元到6,728元不等. 全国经贸中心平均接收额约为2,411美元。 例如,在2021年,有2个孩子的单亲父母本可以得到5,980美元的税收抵免,但收入水平不高。减税额随所得收入增加,最高可达一定数额.挣得的所得税抵免经常受到经济学家和公众的欢迎,因为它有效地增加了工作所得的付款。

p206.original: What about the danger of the poverty trap that every additional $1 earned will reduce government support payments by close to $1? To minimize this problem, the earned income tax credit is phased out slowly. For example, according to the Tax Policy Center, for a single-parent family with two children in 2013, the credit is not reduced at all (but neither is it increased) as earnings rise from $13,430 to $17,530. Then, for every $1 earned above $17,530, the amount received from the credit is reduced by 21.06 cents, until the credit phases out completely at an income level of $46,227.
p206.zh: 贫穷陷阱的危险如何,每增加一美元,政府的支助付款就会减少近一美元? 为尽量减少这一问题,收入所得税抵免额逐步取消。 例如,根据税收政策中心的资料,2013年对有两个孩子的单亲家庭的信贷根本没有减少(但也没有增加),因为收入从13 430美元增加到17 530美元。 然后,每1美元收入超过17 530美元,从信贷中收到的金额减少21.06美分,直到信贷阶段完全结束,收入水平为46 227美元。

p207.original: illustrates that the earned income tax credits, child tax credits, and the TANF program all cost the federal government money—either in direct outlays or in loss of tax revenues. CTC stands for the government tax cuts for the child tax credit.
p207.zh: 说明赚取的收入所得税抵免、儿童税款抵免和TANF方案都使联邦政府付出了费用,无论是直接开支还是税收损失。反恐委员会主张政府削减儿童税收减免。

p208.original: Real Federal Spending on CTC, EITC, and TANF, 1975–2016
p208.zh: 1975-2016年联邦在反恐委员会、国际贸易和外贸司和TANF方面的实际开支

p209.original: In recent years, the EITC has become a hugely expensive government program for providing income assistance to people below or near the poverty line, costing about $60 billion in 2021. In that year, the EITC provided benefits to about 25 million families and individuals and, on average, is worth about $2,411 per family (with children), according to the Tax Policy Center. One reason that the TANF law worked as well as it did is that the government greatly expanded EITC in the late 1980s and again in the early 1990s, which increased the returns to work for low-income Americans.
p209.zh: 近年来,经贸中心已成为一项昂贵的政府方案,向贫困线以下或接近贫困线的人提供收入援助,2021年耗资约600亿美元。 根据税收政策中心的资料,该年,ETC向大约2,500万个家庭和个人提供了福利,平均每个家庭(有子女)价值约为2,411美元。TANF法同样有效的一个原因是,政府在1980年代末和1990年代初大幅扩充了ETC,这增加了低收入美国人的工作回报。

p211.original: Often called “food stamps,” Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) is a federally funded program, started in 1964, in which each month people receive a card like a debit card that they can use to buy food. The amount of food aid for which a household is eligible varies by income, number of children, and other factors but, in general, households are expected to spend about 30% of their own net income on food, and if 30% of their net income is not enough to purchase a nutritionally adequate diet, then those households are eligible for SNAP.
p211.zh: 通常称为“食品邮票”的补充营养援助方案(SNAP)是一个联邦资助的方案,始于1964年,其中人们每月收到一张卡片,如借记卡,可以用来购买食品。家庭有资格获得的粮食援助数额因收入、子女人数和其他因素而异,但一般情况下,家庭将花费其净收入的30%左右用于食品,如果其净收入的30%不足以购买营养充足的饮食,这些家庭就有资格获得国家营养计划。

p212.original: SNAP can contribute to the poverty trap. For every $100 earned, the government assumes that a family can spend $30 more for food, and thus reduces its eligibility for food aid by $30. This decreased benefit is not a complete disincentive to work—but combined with how other programs reduce benefits as income increases, it adds to the problem. SNAP, however, does try to address the poverty trap with its own set of work requirements and time limits.
p212.zh: SNAP可以助长贫困陷阱。 政府每挣100美元,就假定一个家庭可以多花30美元购买食物,从而将获得粮食援助的资格降低了30美元。 这种福利的减少并不是对工作的完全抑制——但加上其他方案如何随着收入的增加而减少福利,这又加剧了问题。 然而,国家农发方案确实试图用自己的一套工作要求和时限来解决贫困问题。

p213.original: Why give debit cards and not just cash? Part of the political support for SNAP comes from a belief that since recipients must spend the  the cards on food, they cannot “waste” them on other forms of consumption. From an economic point of view, however, the belief that cards must increase spending on food seems wrong-headed. After all, say that a family is spending $2,500 per year on food, and then it starts receiving $1,000 per year in SNAP aid. The family might react by spending $3,500 per year on food (income plus aid), or it might react by continuing to spend $2,500 per year on food, but use the $1,000 in food aid to free up $1,000 that it can now spend on other goods. Thus, it is reasonable to think of SNAP cards as an alternative method, along with TANF and the earned income tax credit, of transferring income to those working but still experiencing poverty.
p213.zh: 为什么要给借记卡,而不只是现金? 对SNAP的政治支持部分来自这样一种信念,即由于接受者必须把卡片花在食品上,所以他们不能将卡片“浪费”在其他形式的消费上。 然而,从经济角度来看,认为卡片必须增加粮食开支似乎是错误的。毕竟,一个家庭每年花费2,500美元购买食物,然后它开始每年得到1,000加元的SNAP援助.家庭的反应可能是每年花费3 500美元用于食品(收入加援助),或者它的反应是每年继续花费2 500美元用于食品,但利用粮食援助中的1 000美元腾出1 000美元用于现在可以用于其他商品。 因此,可以合理地认为,SNAP卡与TANF和所得所得税抵免一道,是将收入转移给那些工作但仍在贫穷中的人的另一种方法。

p214.original: Anyone eligible for TANF is also eligible for SNAP, although states can expand eligibility for food aid if they wish to do so. In some states, where TANF welfare spending is relatively low, a poor family may receive more in support from SNAP than from TANF. In 2021, about 41.5 million people received food aid with total benefits of just over $108 billion, which is an average monthly benefit of about $287 per person per month. SNAP participation increased by 70% between 2007 and 2011, from 26.6 million participants to 45 million. According to the Congressional Budget Office, the 2008-2009 Great Recession and rising food prices caused this dramatic rise in participation. Likewise, between 2019 and 2021, the number of participants in SNAP increased by 5.8 million, the amount per person increased by 67%, and total benefits nearly doubled as a consequence of the sharp recession due to the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic in early 2020.
p214.zh: 任何有资格获得国家粮食援助基金的人也有资格获得国家粮食援助方案,尽管各州如果愿意,可以扩大获得粮食援助的资格。在一些邦,在TANF福利支出相对较低的情况下,贫困家庭从SNAP得到的支助可能多于从TANF得到的支助。2021年,约4150万人获得粮食援助,补助总额略高于1 080亿美元,平均每月每人补助287美元。2007年至2011年,国家行动纲领的参与增加了70%,从2 660万人增加到4 500万人。 根据国会预算办公室的资料,2008-2009年大衰退和粮食价格上涨导致参与人数急剧上升。 同样,在2019年至2021年间,由于2020年初COVID-19大流行爆发导致的急剧衰退,SNAP的参与者人数增加了580万人,人均受益额增加了67%,总福利几乎翻了一番.

p215.original: The federal government deploys a range of income security programs that it funds through departments such as Health and Human Services, Agriculture, and Housing and Urban Development (HUD) (see ). According to the Office of Management and Budget, collectively, these three departments provided an estimated $62 billion of aid through programs such as supplemental feeding programs for women and children, subsidized housing, and energy assistance. The federal government also transfers funds to individual states through special grant programs.
p215.zh: 联邦政府通过卫生与公众服务、农业、住房和城市发展等部门,实施了一系列收入保障方案(见)。 根据管理和预算办公室的资料,这三个部门通过诸如妇女和儿童补充供餐方案、住房补贴和能源援助等方案,共同提供了约620亿美元的援助。联邦政府还通过特别赠款方案向各州转移资金。

p216.original: Expenditure Comparison of TANF, SNAP, HUD, and Other Income Security Programs, 1988–2013 (est.)
p216.zh: 1988-2013年TANF、SNAP、HUD和其他收入保障方案支出比较(最高)

p217.original: The safety net includes a number of other programs: government-subsidized school lunches and breakfasts for children from low-income families; the Special Supplemental Food Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC), which provides food assistance for pregnant women and newborns; the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, which provides help with home heating bills; housing assistance, which helps pay the rent; and Supplemental Security Income, which provides cash support for people with disabilities and elderly people experiencing poverty.
p217.zh: 安全网包括若干其他方案:政府补贴的低收入家庭儿童的学校午餐和早餐;向孕妇和新生儿提供粮食援助的妇女、婴儿和儿童特别补充食品方案;为家庭供暖费提供帮助的低收入家庭能源援助方案;帮助支付租金的住房援助;以及向残疾人和贫穷老人提供现金支助的补充安全收入。

p219.original: Congress created Medicaid in 1965. This is a joint health insurance program between both the states and the federal government. The federal government helps fund Medicaid, but each state is responsible for administering the program, determining the level of benefits, and determining eligibility. It provides medical insurance for certain people with low incomes, including those below the poverty line, with a focus on families with children, the elderly, and people with disabilities. About one-third of Medicaid spending is for low-income mothers with children. While an increasing share of the program funding in recent years has gone to pay for nursing home costs for older people who cannot afford to pay for housing. The program ensures that participants receive a basic level of benefits, but because each state sets eligibility requirements and provides varying levels of service, the program differs from state to state.
p219.zh: 1965年,国会创建了"医疗救助计划"(Medicaid). 这是各州和联邦政府的联合健康保险方案。联邦政府帮助为医疗补助提供资金,但每个州都负责管理方案,确定福利水平,并确定资格. 它向某些低收入的人,包括生活在贫困线以下的人提供医疗保险,重点是有子女、老人和残疾人的家庭。大约三分之一的医药援助开支用于有子女的低收入母亲。 虽然近年来方案资金中越来越多的份额用于支付无力支付住房费用的老年人的养老院费用。 该方案确保参与者获得基本水平的福利,但由于每个州都规定了资格要求并提供不同水平的服务,该方案因州而异.

p220.original: In the past, a common problem has been that many low-paying jobs pay enough to a breadwinner so that a family could lose its eligibility for Medicaid, yet the job does not offer health insurance benefits. A parent considering such a job might choose not to work rather than lose health insurance for their children. In this way, health insurance can become a part of the poverty trap. Many states recognized this problem in the 1980s and 1990s and expanded their Medicaid coverage to include people earning up to 135% or even 185% of the poverty line. Some states also guaranteed that children would not lose coverage if their parents worked.
p220.zh: 过去的一个常见问题是,许多低薪工作向养家糊口者支付足够的工资,使一个家庭丧失获得医疗补助的资格,然而该工作却不提供健康保险福利。考虑从事这种工作的父母可能选择不工作,而不是失去其子女的健康保险。 这样,健康保险就可以成为贫穷陷阱的一部分。 许多州在1980年代和1990年代都认识到这一问题,并扩大了医疗补助的覆盖面,将收入最高达贫困线的135%甚至185%的人包括在内。 一些州还保证,如果父母工作,儿童不会失去保险。

p221.original: These expanded guarantees cost the government money, of course, but they also helped to encourage those on welfare to enter the labor force. As of 2014, approximately 69.7 million people participated in Medicaid. Of those enrolled, almost half are children. Healthcare expenditures, however, are highest for the elderly population, which comprises approximately 25% of participants. As  (a) indicates, the largest number of households that enroll in Medicaid are those with children. Lower-income adults are the next largest group enrolled in Medicaid at 38%. People who are blind or have a disability account for 15% of those enrolled, and seniors are 8% of those enrolled.  (b) shows how much actual Medicaid dollars the government spends for each group. Out of total Medicaid spending, the government spends more on seniors (20%) and people who are blind or have a disability (44%). Thus, 64% of all Medicaid spending goes to seniors, those who are blind, and people with disabilities. Children receive 21% of all Medicaid spending, followed by adults at 15%.
p221.zh: 这些扩大的担保当然要花政府的钱,但也有助于鼓励福利人员加入劳动力队伍。 截至2014年,约有6 970万人参加了医疗救助计划。 在注册的学员中,近一半是儿童。 然而,老年人口的保健支出最高,约占参与者的25%。 如(a)所示,接受医疗补助的家庭数量最多,是那些有孩子的家庭。低收入成年人是接受医疗补助的第二大群体,占38%。盲人或残疾者占注册人数的15%,老年人占注册人数的8%。(b) 说明政府为每一群体实际花费多少医疗补助。 在医疗补助的总支出中,政府对老年人(20%)和盲人或残疾人(44%)的支出更多。 因此,所有医疗补助开支的64%用于老年人、盲人和残疾人。儿童获得所有医疗补助开支的21%,其次是成年人,占15%。

p222.zh: 医疗补助的注册和开支

p224.original: We call the group of government programs that address poverty the safety net. In the United States, prominent safety net programs include Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF), the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), the earned income tax credit (EITC), Medicaid, and the Special Supplemental Food Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC).
p224.zh: 我们把解决贫穷问题的政府方案小组称为安全网。在美国,突出的安全网方案包括向贫困家庭提供临时援助、补充营养援助方案、收入所得税抵免、医疗补助和妇女、婴儿和儿童特别补充食品方案。

p226.original: We have discovered that the welfare system discourages recipients from working because the more income they earn, the less welfare benefits they receive. How does the earned income tax credit attempt to loosen the poverty trap?
p226.zh: 我们发现,福利制度阻止领取者工作,因为他们的收入越多,领取的福利福利就越少。所得所得税抵免如何试图放松贫困陷阱?

p227.original: The earned income tax credit works like this: a family receives a tax break that increases according to how much they work. Families that work more get more. In that sense it loosens the poverty trap by encouraging work. As families earn above the poverty level, the earned income tax credit is gradually reduced. For those near-poor families, the earned income tax credit is a partial disincentive to work.
p227.zh: 所得所得税抵免办法就是这样工作的:家庭可按其工作量获得增税。工作较多的家庭会得到更多。 从这个意义上说,它通过鼓励工作来缓解贫困陷阱。 随着家庭收入高于贫困水平,所得所得税抵免逐渐减少. 对于那些接近贫穷的家庭,所得所得税抵免是部分妨碍工作的因素。

p228.original: How does the TANF attempt to loosen the poverty trap?
p228.zh: TANF如何试图放松贫困陷阱?

p229.original: TANF attempts to loosen the poverty trap by providing incentives to work in other ways. Specifically, it requires that people work (or complete their education) as a condition of receiving TANF benefits, and it places a time limit on benefits.
p229.zh: TANF试图通过提供以其他方式工作的奖励来缓解贫困陷阱。具体地说,它要求人们工作(或完成教育)作为领取TANF福利的条件,它规定了福利的时限.

p232.original: Briefly explain the differences between TANF, the earned income tax credit, SNAP, and Medicaid.
p232.zh: 简要地解释TANF、所得所得税抵免、SNAP和医疗补助之间的差别。

p234.original: Many critics of government programs to help low-income individuals argue that these programs create a poverty trap. Explain how programs such as TANF, EITC, SNAP, and Medicaid will affect low-income individuals and whether or not you think these programs will benefit families and children.
p234.zh: 许多批评政府帮助低收入个人的方案的人认为,这些方案造成了贫困陷阱。解释诸如TANF、EITC、SNAP和Medicaid等方案将如何影响低收入个人,以及你是否认为这些方案将使家庭和儿童受益。

p235.original: Think about the business cycle: during a recession, unemployment increases; it decreases in an expansionary phase. Explain what happens to TANF, SNAP, and Medicaid programs at each phase of the business cycle (recession, trough, expansion, and peak).

p242.zh: 收入不平等:衡量和原因

p243.original: Poverty levels can be subjective based on the overall income levels of a country. Typically a government measures poverty based on a percentage of the median income. Income inequality, however, has to do with the distribution of that income, in terms of which group receives the most or the least income. Income inequality involves comparing those with high incomes, middle incomes, and low incomes—not just looking at those below or near the poverty line. In turn, measuring income inequality means dividing the population into various groups and then comparing the groups, a task that we can be carry out in several ways, as the next Clear It Up feature shows.
p243.zh: 贫穷程度可能基于一个国家的总体收入水平而主观。通常,政府根据中等收入的百分比衡量贫穷。 然而,收入不平等与收入的分配有关,从哪个群体获得的收入最多或最少。收入不平等涉及比较高收入、中等收入和低收入者,而不只是看贫困线以下或接近贫困线者。反过来,衡量收入不平等意味着将人口分成不同的群体,然后比较这些群体,正如下一个“明确起来”特征所示,我们可以以几种方式完成这项任务。

p244.original: How do you separate poverty and income inequality?
p244.zh: 如何区分贫困和收入不平等?

p245.original: Poverty can change even when inequality does not move at all. Imagine a situation in which income for everyone in the population declines by 10%. Poverty would rise, since a greater share of the population would now fall below the poverty line. However, inequality would be the same, because everyone suffered the same proportional loss. Conversely, a general rise in income levels over time would keep inequality the same, but reduce poverty.
p245.zh: 即使在不平等完全不动的情况下,贫穷也可能改变。想象一下,人口中每个人的收入都下降了10%。贫穷将增加,因为现在更多的人口将降到贫困线以下。 然而,不平等将是一样的,因为每个人都遭受了同样比例的损失。 相反,收入水平随时间推移而普遍提高,将维持不平等,但减少贫穷。

p246.original: It is also possible for income inequality to change without affecting the poverty rate. Imagine a situation in which a large number of people who already have high incomes increase their incomes by even more. Inequality would rise as a result—but the number of people below the poverty line would remain unchanged.
p246.zh: 收入不平等也有可能发生变化,而不影响贫困率。想象一下,许多已经高收入的人的收入会增加更多。不平等将因此而加剧,但贫困线以下的人数将保持不变。

p247.original: Why did inequality of household income increase in the United States in recent decades? A trend toward greater income inequality has occurred in many countries around the world, although the effect has been more powerful in the U.S. economy. Economists have focused their explanations for the increasing inequality on two factors that changed more or less continually from the 1970s into the 2000s. One set of explanations focuses on the changing shape of American households. The other focuses on greater inequality of wages, what some economists call “winner take all” labor markets. We will begin with how we measure inequality, and then consider the explanations for growing inequality in the United States.
p247.zh: 美国近几十年来,家庭收入的不平等为何增加?世界上许多国家都出现了收入不平等加剧的趋势,尽管这种影响在美国经济中更为强大。经济学家将不平等日益加剧的解释集中在两个因素上,这两个因素从1970年代到2000年代或多或少地不断发生变化。 有一套解释侧重于美国家庭的形态变化.另一种观点则强调工资更加不平等,一些经济学家称之为“赢家全拿”的劳动力市场。 我们首先要考虑我们如何衡量不平等,然后考虑美国日益不平等的原因。

p248.zh: 按昆蒂莱斯计算收入分配

p249.original: One common way of measuring income inequality is to rank all households by income, from lowest to highest, and then to divide all households into five groups with equal numbers of people, known as quintiles. This calculation allows for measuring the distribution of income among the five groups compared to the total. The first quintile is the lowest fifth or 20%, the second quintile is the next lowest, and so on. We can measure income inequality by comparing what share of the total income each quintile earns.
p249.zh: 衡量收入不平等的一个常见方法是按收入划分所有家庭的等级,从最低到最高,然后将所有家庭分为人口相等的五组,称为五分位数. 这一计算可以衡量五类收入与总额之间的分配。 第一五等分层为最低五等分层或20%,第二五等分层为第二五等分层等. 我们可以通过比较每五分之一收入在总收入中所占的份额来衡量收入不平等。

p250.original: U.S. income distribution by quintile appears in . In 2020, for example, the bottom quintile of the income distribution received 3.2% of income; the second quintile received 8.1%; the third quintile, 14.0%; the fourth quintile, 22.6%; and the top quintile, 52.2%. The final column of  shows what share of income went to households in the top 5% of the income distribution: 23.0% in 2020. Over time, from the late 1960s to the early 1980s, the top fifth of the income distribution typically received between about 43% to 44% of all income. The share of income that the top fifth received then begins to rise. Census Bureau researchers trace, much of this increase in the share of income going to the top fifth to an increase in the share of income going to the top 5%. The quintile measure shows how income inequality has increased in recent decades.
p250.zh: 美国按五分位数划分的收入分配情况见......。 例如,在2020年,收入分配中,收入分配的底层五分之一获得3.2%的收入;第二层五分之一获得8.1%的收入;第三层五分之一获得14.0%的收入;第四层五分之一获得22.6%的收入;第五层五分之一获得52.2%。 最后一栏显示收入分配额中最高5%的家庭的收入份额:2020年为23.0%。随着时间的推移,从1960年代末到1980年代初,收入分配中排名前五者一般获得收入总额的43%至44%。排名前五者的收入份额开始上升。人口普查局的研究人员追踪到,收入份额增长的大部分会上升到前五,收入份额增长到前5%。 五分位数衡量标准表明,近几十年来收入不平等状况如何加剧。

p251.original: Share of Aggregate Income Received by Each Fifth and Top 5% of Households, 1967–2020
p251.zh: 1967-2020年每5户和前5%家庭获得的总收入份额

p343.original: It can also be useful to divide the income distribution in ways other than quintiles; for example, into tenths or even into percentiles (that is, hundredths). A more detailed breakdown can provide additional insights. For example, the last column of  shows the income received by the top 5% of the income distribution. Between 1980 and 2020, the share of income going to the top 5% increased by 6.5 percentage points (from 16.5% in 1980 to 23.0% in 2020). From 1980 to 2020 the share of income going to the top quintile increased by 8.1 percentage points (from 44.1% in 1980 to 52.2% in 2013). Thus, the top 20% of householders (the fifth quintile) received over half (51%) of all the income in the United States in 2020.
p343.zh: 此外,还可以将收入分配除五分位数之外的其他方式加以划分;例如,分成十分之一甚至百分位数(即百分位数)。更详细的细分可以提供更多的见解。 例如,最后一栏显示收入分配额前5%收到的收入。 在1980年至2020年期间,收入占前5%的比例增加了6.5个百分点(从1980年的16.5%增加到2020年的23.0%)。 从1980年到2020年,五分位居前列的收入份额增加了8.1个百分点(从1980年的44.1%增至2013年的52.2%)。 因此,前20%的住户(五分之一)在2020年获得美国所有收入的一半以上(51%)。

p345.original: We can present the data on income inequality in various ways. For example, you could draw a bar graph that showed the share of income going to each fifth of the income distribution.  presents an alternative way of showing inequality data in a Lorenz curve. This curve shows the cumulative share of population on the horizontal axis and the cumulative percentage of total income received on the vertical axis.
p345.zh: 我们可以以各种方式提供收入不平等的数据。 例如,您可以绘制一个条形图,显示收入分配的五分之一。它提供了一种以洛伦兹曲线显示不平等数据的替代方式。 该曲线显示横向轴上人口累积比例和纵向轴上总收入的累积百分比.

p347.original: Every Lorenz curve diagram begins with a line sloping up at a 45-degree angle. We show it as a dashed line in . The points along this line show what perfect equality of the income distribution looks like. It would mean, for example, that the bottom 20% of the income distribution receives 20% of the total income, the bottom 40% gets 40% of total income, and so on. The other lines reflect actual U.S. data on inequality for 1980 and 2020.
p347.zh: 每个洛伦兹曲线图都以45度角的直线向上延伸为起点。 我们把它看成一条破烂的线沿着这条线的要点表明,收入分配的完美平等是什么样的。举例来说,这意味着收入分配的下20%获得总收入的20%,下40%获得总收入的40%,等等。 其他线路反映了美国1980年和2020年关于不平等的实际数据.

p348.original: The trick in graphing a Lorenz curve is that you must change the shares of income for each specific quintile, which we show in the first and third columns of numbers in , into cumulative income, which we show in the second and fourth columns of numbers. For example, the bottom 40% of the cumulative income distribution will be the sum of the first and second quintiles; the bottom 60% of the cumulative income distribution will be the sum of the first, second, and third quintiles, and so on. The final entry in the cumulative income column needs to be 100%, because by definition, 100% of the population receives 100% of the income.
p348.zh: 绘制一个洛伦兹曲线的技巧是, 你必须改变每个特定五分位数的收入份额, 我们在第一和第三列数字中显示, 变成累积收入, 我们在第二和第四列数字中显示。 例如,在累计收入分配中,收入分配的下40%将是第一和第二五分位数的总和;收入分配的下60%是第一、第二和第三五分位数的总和,等等。累计收入栏的最后条目需要达到100%,因为按照定义,100%的人口获得100%的收入.

p380.original: In a Lorenz curve diagram, a more unequal distribution of income will loop farther down and away from the 45-degree line, while a more equal distribution of income will move the line closer to the 45-degree line.  illustrates the greater inequality of the U.S. income distribution between 1980 and 2020 because the Lorenz curve for 2020 is farther from the 45-degree line than the Lorenz curve for 1980. The Lorenz curve is a useful way of presenting the quintile data that provides an image of all the quintile data at once. The next Clear It Up feature shows how income inequality differs in various countries compared to the United States.
p380.zh: 在洛伦兹曲线图中,收入分配更加不平等将更远地向下和远离45度线,而收入分配更加平等则会使线路更接近45度线. 说明1980年至2020年间美国收入分配更加不平等,因为2020年的洛伦兹曲线比1980年的洛伦兹曲线离45度线更远.洛伦兹曲线是一种有用的方法,可以同时显示所有五分位数数据的图像。下一个Clear It Up的特征显示,与美国相比,各国收入不平等的情况如何。

p381.original: How does economic inequality vary around the world?
p381.zh: 经济不平等在世界各地有何不同?

p382.original: The U.S. economy has a relatively high degree of income inequality by global standards. As  shows, based on a variety of national surveys for a selection of years in the second decade of this century, the U.S. economy has greater inequality than Germany (along with most Western European countries). The region of the world with the highest level of income inequality is Latin America, illustrated in the numbers for Brazil and Mexico. The level of inequality in the United States is higher than in some of the low-income countries of the world, like India and Nigeria, as well as in some middle-income countries, like China and Russia.
p382.zh: 按全球标准计算,美国经济的收入不平等程度相对较高. 如所显示,根据本世纪第二个十年中若干年份的各种全国性调查,美国经济比德国(与大多数西欧国家一样)有更大的不平等.世界上收入不平等程度最高的区域是拉丁美洲,巴西和墨西哥的数字就说明了这一点。 美国的不平等程度高于世界上一些低收入国家,如印度和尼日利亚,以及一些中等收入国家,如中国和俄罗斯.

p447.zh: 访问该网站观看全球财富不平等的视频.

p448.original: Causes of Growing Inequality: The Changing Composition of American Households
p448.zh: 日益不平等的原因:美国家庭组成的变化

p449.original: In 1970, 41% of married women were in the labor force, but by 2019, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, 58.6% of married women were in the labor force. One result of this trend is that more households have two earners. Moreover, it has become more common for one high earner to marry another high earner. A few decades ago, the common pattern featured a man with relatively high earnings, such as an executive or a doctor, marrying a woman who did not earn as much, like a secretary or a nurse. Often, the woman would leave paid employment, at least for a few years, to raise a family. However, now doctors are marrying doctors and executives are marrying executives, and mothers with high-powered careers are often returning to work while their children are quite young. This pattern of households with two high earners tends to increase the proportion of high-earning households.
p449.zh: 1970年,41%的已婚妇女在劳动力队伍中,但据劳动统计局统计,到2019年,58.6%的已婚妇女在劳动力队伍中.这一趋势的一个结果是,更多的家庭有两个收入者。 此外,一个高收入者与另一个高收入者结婚已变得更加普遍。几十年前,一个收入相对较高的男子,如行政官员或医生,与一个收入不如秘书或护士这样的妇女结婚,成为常见的典型。妇女往往为了养育家庭而离开有薪工作,至少几年。 然而,现在医生正在与医生结婚,而高管正在与高管结婚,事业能力强的母亲往往在孩子还很年轻的时候返回工作岗位. 这种收入高的住户模式往往会增加高收入住户的比例。

p450.original: According to data in the National Journal, even as two-earner couples have increased, so have single-parent households. Of all U.S. families, in 2021, about 23% were headed by single mothers. The poverty rate among single-parent households tends to be relatively high.
p450.zh: 根据"全国日报"的数据,即使双耳夫妇增多,单亲家庭也有所增加.在美国所有家庭当中,2021年,大约23%的户主是单身母亲.单亲家庭的贫困率往往相对较高。

p451.original: These changes in family structure, including the growth of single-parent families who tend to be at the lower end of the income distribution, and the growth of two-career high-earner couples near the top end of the income distribution, account for roughly half of the rise in income inequality across households in recent decades.
p451.zh: 家庭结构的这些变化,包括往往处于收入分配较低端的单亲家庭的增长,以及接近收入分配最高端的双职工高龄夫妇的增长,约占近几十年来家庭收入不平等增加的一半。

p452.zh: 访问这个网站观看一段显示美国财富分配的视频.

p453.original: Causes of Growing Inequality: A Shift in the Distribution of Wages
p453.zh: 日益不平等的原因:工资分配的转变

p454.original: Another factor behind the rise in U.S. income inequality is that earnings have become less equal since the late 1970s. In particular, the earnings of high-skilled labor relative to low-skilled labor have increased. Winner-take-all labor markets result from changes in technology, which have increased global demand for “stars,”—whether the best CEO, doctor, basketball player, or actor. This global demand pushes salaries far above productivity differences associated with educational differences. One way to measure this change is to take workers' earnings with at least a four-year college bachelor’s degree (including those who went on and completed an advanced degree) and divide them by workers' earnings with only a high school degree. The result is that those in the 25–34 age bracket with college degrees earned about 1.85 times as much as high school graduates in 2020, up from 1.59 times in 1995, according to U.S. Census data. Winner-take-all labor market theory argues that the salary gap between the median and the top 1 percent is not due to educational differences.
p454.zh: 美国收入不平等加剧的另一个因素是,自1970年代末以来,收入的均等程度降低。特别是,高技能劳动力相对于低技能劳动力的收入有所增加。获得胜利的劳动力市场是技术变化的结果,这些变化增加了全球对“明星”的需求,无论是最佳首席执行官、医生、篮球运动员还是演员。 这一全球需求使薪金远远超出与教育差异相关的生产力差异。衡量这一变化的一个方法是将至少四年的大学学士学位的工人收入(包括继续学习并完成高级学位的工人)除以只有高中学位的工人收入。结果是,根据美国的数据,25-34岁年龄段的大学学位学生在2020年的收入是高中毕业生的1.85倍,比1995年的1.59倍有所增加。人口普查数据。中位数和最高1%之间的工资差距不是教育差异造成的。

p455.original: Economists use the demand and supply model to reason through the most likely causes of this shift. According to the National Center for Education Statistics, in recent decades, the supply of U.S. workers with college degrees has increased substantially. For example, 840,000 four-year bachelor’s degrees were conferred on Americans in 1970. In 2018–2019, 2.0 million such degrees were conferred—an increase of over 138%. In , this shift in supply to the right, from S0 to S1, by itself should result in a lower equilibrium wage for high-skilled labor. Thus, we can explain the increase in the price of high-skilled labor by a greater demand, like the movement from D0 to D1. Evidently, combining both the increase in supply and in demand has resulted in a shift from E0 to E1, and a resulting higher wage.
p455.zh: 经济学家利用供求模式来解释这种转变的最可能原因。 据国家教育统计中心统计,近几十年来,美国拥有大学学位的工人供应量大幅增加. 例如,1970年授予美国人84万个四年制学士学位。2018-2019年,授予了200万个此类学位——增加了138%以上。供应向右的这一转变,从S0到S1, 本身就会导致高技能劳动力的平衡工资降低。 因此,我们可以用更大的需求来解释高技能劳动力价格上涨的原因,比如从D0到D1的移动. 显然,供需两者的结合,导致了E0向E1的转变,并导致工资的提高。

p456.original: Why Would Wages Rise for High-Skilled Labor?
p456.zh: 为什么高技能劳工的工资会上升?

p457.original: What factors would cause the demand for high-skilled labor to rise? The most plausible explanation is that while the explosion in new information and communications technologies over the last several decades has helped many workers to become more productive, the benefits have been especially great for high-skilled workers like top business managers, consultants, and design professionals. The new technologies have also helped to encourage globalization, the remarkable increase in international trade over the last few decades, by making it more possible to learn about and coordinate economic interactions all around the world. In turn, the rising impact of foreign trade in the U.S. economy has opened up greater opportunities for high-skilled workers to sell their services around the world, and lower-skilled workers have to compete with a larger supply of similarly skilled workers around the globe.
p457.zh: 哪些因素会导致对高技能劳动力的需求上升? 最有道理的解释是,尽管过去几十年中新信息和通信技术的爆炸帮助了许多工人提高了生产率,但对于高技能工人来说,如顶级企业经理、顾问和设计专业人员,好处特别大。新技术还帮助鼓励全球化,使全世界更容易了解和协调经济互动,从而鼓励了过去几十年国际贸易的显著增长。反过来,对外贸易在美国经济中的影响越来越大,为高技能工人在世界各地出售服务提供了更多机会,低技能工人必须和全球更多类似技术工人的供给竞争.

p458.original: We can view the market for high-skilled labor as a race between forces of supply and demand. Additional education and on-the-job training will tend to increase the high-skilled labor supply and to hold down its relative wage. Conversely, new technology and other economic trends like globalization tend to increase the demand for high-skilled labor and push up its relative wage. We can view the greater inequality of wages as a sign that demand for skilled labor is increasing faster than supply. Alternatively, if the supply of lower skilled workers exceeds the demand, then average wages in the lower quintiles of the income distribution will decrease. The combination of forces in the high-skilled and low-skilled labor markets leads to increased income disparity.
p458.zh: 我们可以把高技能劳动力的市场看作是供求力量之间的竞争。额外的教育和在职培训往往会增加高技能劳动力的供应,并降低其相对工资。 相反,新技术和全球化等其他经济趋势往往会增加对高技能劳动力的需求,并提高其相对工资。 我们可以将工资不平等的加剧视为技术劳动力需求增长快于供应的一个迹象。 或者,如果低技能工人的供应超过需求,那么收入分配的低五分位人口的平均工资将下降。高技能劳动力市场和低技能劳动力市场的力量组合导致收入差距扩大。

p460.original: Measuring inequality involves making comparisons across the entire distribution of income. One way of doing this is to divide the population into groups, like quintiles, and then calculate what share of income each group receives. An alternative approach is to draw Lorenz curves, which compare the cumulative income actually received to a perfectly equal distribution of income. Income inequality in the United States increased substantially from the late 1970s and early 1980s into the 2000s. The two most common explanations that economists cite are changes in household structures that have led to more two-earner couples and single-parent families, and the effect of new information and communications technology on wages.
p460.zh: 衡量不平等需要对整个收入分配进行比较。这样做的一种方法是将人口分成五分位数等群体,然后计算每个群体获得的收入份额。另一种办法是绘制洛伦兹曲线,将实际收到的累积收入与完全平等的收入分配进行比较。 从1970年代末和1980年代初到2000年代,美国的收入不平等程度大幅上升。经济学家最常提到的两种解释是,家庭结构的变化导致更多的双耳夫妇和单亲家庭,以及新的信息和通信技术对工资的影响。

p466.original: Using two demand and supply diagrams, one for the low-wage labor market and one for the high-wage labor market, explain how information technology can increase income inequality if it is a complement to high-income workers like salespeople and managers, but a substitute for low-income workers like file clerks and telephone receptionists.

p467.original: In the market for low-wage labor, information technology shifts the demand for low-wage labor to the left. One reason is that technology can often substitute for low-wage labor in certain kinds of telephone or bookkeeping jobs. In addition, information technology makes it easier for companies to manage connections with low-wage workers in other countries, thus reducing the demand for low-wage workers in the United States. In the market for high-wage labor, information technology shifts the demand for high-wage labor to the right. By using the new information and communications technologies, high-wage labor can become more productive and can oversee more tasks than before. The following figure illustrates these two labor markets. The combination of lower wages for low-wage labor and higher wages for high-wage labor means greater inequality.
